Adriana, thank you for making the time. I have read your profile, and Karen has told me a lot about you.
Thank you for the invitation. I have been looking forward to this conversation.
Let us start with the classic one. Tell me about yourself.

My background is in organizational pedagogy, and I have worked in human resources for more than twenty years. I have led the area for a global logistics company, and I have rolled out programs that the head office in Germany later adopted.
That is a strong track record. What is the scope you have managed so far?
Climate, litigation, benefits, succession and the cost of the workforce. I reported to a director in the United States, so most of that work has already happened in English.
Good. Now something that is not on your profile. What is the worst decision you have ever made about people?
That is a fair question. I kept a manager in a role for a whole year after the team had told me the problem. I have never made that mistake again.

Hello Adriana, this is Karen Whitfield from the talent team. I am calling about the HR director position. We have received your profile and the whole panel has read it, so thank you for that. I would like to schedule the first conversation for Thursday, at four in the afternoon, Brazilian time. It is a thirty minute call in English with me and with the regional vice president. We are not going to test your technical knowledge. We already know your background. What we want to hear is how you talk about your work: what you have led, what you have changed, and what you have learned along the way. There is no presentation, so please do not prepare slides. Just be ready to talk. Call me back today if Thursday does not work for you. Thank you, and have a good afternoon.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the regional leadership meeting. For the people who have joined us this quarter, my name is Paul Renner and I lead human resources for the Americas. My background is not in human resources. I studied engineering, I spent nine years in operations, and I moved to this area almost by accident, because somebody had to fix a plant where nobody wanted to work. I have been in HR since then, and I have never regretted it. Today my team supports fourteen thousand people in eleven countries. I have rolled out three global programs, and I can tell you that the second one failed completely. We have learned more from that one than from the other two together. So when you present your numbers today, please do not hide the ones that did not work. That is not what this meeting is for.
